# General Readiness Checklist: OpenAPI Specification Engine

**Purpose**: Balanced, pre-`/speckit-tasks` review of requirements quality across the spec, plan, research, and data model for AP-002 — completeness, clarity, consistency, and edge-case coverage.
**Created**: 2026-08-26
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is inheritance of a top-level/global `security` requirement to operations that declare no operation-level security explicitly addressed in the requirements? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements defined for how the analysis summary or UI should behave while a large specification is still being processed (a loading/in-progress state)? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the structure of extracted `examples` defined for operations with multiple examples per content type, or only a single example assumed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK004 Are UX/display requirements defined for specifications with a very large number of discovered operations (e.g., pagination, grouping)? [Gap, Spec §FR-017]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is the exact maximum upload file size a testable, stated value in the specification itself, rather than only "documented" or left to the plan/research phase? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "well-formed" (as used in SC-002/SC-005) defined precisely enough to distinguish an accepted-with-issues specification from a rejected one? [Clarity, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the boundary between "typical" (50-100 operations, SC-001) and larger specifications clarified — does the 30-second target apply only up to that scale, or without an upper bound? [Clarity, Spec §SC-001]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK008 Is per-content-type schema extraction (as modeled in data-model.md's `RequestBody`/`Response.contentTypes`) consistent with how FR-008/FR-009 describe request/response schema extraction? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008 vs data-model.md]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the "no persistence" decision (research.md) reflected back into the specification's Assumptions, or does it only exist in the plan/research artifacts? [Consistency, Spec Assumptions vs research.md]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK010 Can SC-004 ("determine... whether a specification was fully or only partially understood") be objectively verified, or does it need a more concrete, observable acceptance criterion (e.g., a specific indicator)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK011 Can SC-005 ("zero fabricated endpoints/parameters/fields") be verified through a defined, repeatable check, or does it rely solely on manual inspection? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK012 Are requirements defined for a specification that is syntactically valid JSON (which is also valid YAML) but intended as an OpenAPI document — is JSON-formatted input explicitly detected and rejected, or could it pass through as accepted? [Gap, Spec §FR-001 vs Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements defined for partial/incremental feedback if analysis of a large specification approaches the SC-001 time target without completing? [Gap, Spec §SC-001]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK014 Is a maximum `$ref` resolution depth or timeout specified for deeply nested (but non-circular) reference chains, distinct from the circular-reference case already covered? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the duplicate `operationId`/path+method edge case explicitly cross-referenced to the functional requirement that governs how it is reported (FR-013), rather than appearing only in Edge Cases? [Traceability, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements defined for specifications containing extension fields (`x-*` vendor extensions) — are they ignored, preserved, or flagged? [Gap]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK017 Are concurrency/thread-safety expectations defined for the in-memory analysis pipeline given the single-local-user assumption (e.g., is exactly one analysis processed at a time)? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK018 Are there requirements bounding memory usage for large specifications, given the in-memory-only processing decision? [Gap, research.md "No persistence"]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK019 Is the ~10 MB default file-size assumption validated against realistic large enterprise OpenAPI specifications, or is it an arbitrary placeholder pending confirmation? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the dependency on AP-001's backend/frontend foundation (workspaces, HTTP server, UI shell) explicitly confirmed as satisfied before this feature's requirements can be implemented? [Dependency]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK021 Is the list of "unsupported OpenAPI constructs" (FR-013) enumerated anywhere, or is it left entirely to implementation discretion to decide what counts as unsupported? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK022 Do FR-004 (reject invalid/unsupported specs) and FR-013 (flag ambiguous constructs within an otherwise accepted spec) have a clear, non-overlapping boundary — i.e., is it unambiguous which failures cause outright rejection versus which become flagged issues in an accepted result? [Conflict, Spec §FR-004 vs FR-013]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
